items.title: Outbox states lack transition and field-coherence invariants
items.statement: The schema enumerates pending, published, acked, and failed but does not define legal transitions, terminality, or conditional requirements. It therefore accepts contradictory rows such as acked without publication identifiers, pending with publication identifiers, or failed without error and retry state.
items.impact: Consumers cannot distinguish a valid durable state from a structurally valid but impossible state, undermining replay and recovery.
items.builder_discretion: Define a transition matrix plus status-dependent required, forbidden, and immutable fields.

items.title: Dual-store publication has no crash-consistency protocol
items.statement: The outbox is declared to span redb and seglog, but the contract gives no ordering, atomicity boundary, reconciliation cursor, or recovery behavior for crashes between the durable row mutation and EventRecord append.
items.impact: A crash can plausibly create lost publications, duplicate EventRecords, or rows whose status disagrees with the append-only log.
items.builder_discretion: Specify the commit/append order, durable comparison key, crash points, retry ownership, and reconciliation oracle.

evidence.exact_quote: "legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status": "Canonical PlanApproved transactional outbox row; PlanApproved EventRecord remains the append-only publication.",

items.title: Idempotency replay is not bound to command identity
items.statement: The key uses project_id and an arbitrary non-empty idempotency_key, while replay promises an existing result. No request or payload fingerprint is persisted, so reuse of a key for a different approved pack or compile run has no specified conflict behavior.
items.impact: A collision or malicious key reuse may return a success for a different approval command and silently bind the wrong pack or compile run.
items.builder_discretion: Persist a canonical command digest and require equality before replay; define a typed conflict on mismatch.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Duplicate approval delivery returns the existing PlanApproved append/projection result for the same idempotency key.",

items.title: Outbox ordering and worker concurrency are unconstrained
items.statement: outbox_sequence has only a lower bound. The registry does not state its uniqueness scope, monotonic allocation authority, relation to published_sequence_id, compare-and-swap rules, or worker claim and lease protocol.
items.impact: Concurrent approvals or retry workers can race, publish twice, acknowledge the wrong sequence, or observe inconsistent ordering.
items.builder_discretion: Define allocation scope, unique constraints, mutation CAS token, and single-owner or leased processing semantics.

items.title: Approved pack key omits the declared version
items.statement: The family stores pack_version but keys only by project and approved_plan_pack_id. The contract does not say whether an identifier is immutable, overwritten in place, or paired with a new identifier for every version, and supersedes_pack_id is optional and nullable.
items.impact: Concurrent approval or refresh can overwrite history, make exact replay nondeterministic, or break receipt reachability.
items.builder_discretion: Make immutable identity explicit and include version or an immutable content identity in the key/CAS rules.

items.title: Integrity hashes accept arbitrary non-empty strings
items.statement: pack_hash and the index, context, policy, and closure hash fields are validated only by minLength. Algorithm, encoding, byte domain, length, and normalization are unspecified.
items.impact: Malformed or ambiguous digests can pass schema validation, defeat stale-input checks, and prevent interoperable verification.
items.builder_discretion: Specify a digest algorithm and canonical lowercase encoding or use an algorithm-tagged digest type with exact patterns.

items.title: Reference collections are unbounded and weakly typed
items.statement: Source and lineage reference arrays have no maximum count, byte length, uniqueness rule, or reference grammar. Several optional reference strings also allow empty values, despite the required source_refs items requiring minLength one.
items.impact: Oversized or duplicate arrays can amplify storage and decode cost, while malformed or empty refs become unusable lineage and recovery pointers.
items.builder_discretion: Define bounded canonical reference types, maximum cardinalities and lengths, and uniqueness/order semantics.

items.title: Persisted authority is an unauthenticated free-form reference
items.statement: ApprovedPlanPack records require created_by_actor_ref but constrain it only to a non-empty string, with no principal namespace, authorization decision receipt, tenant binding, or immutable approval authority. The outbox row carries no actor or authorization field at all.
items.impact: A structurally valid record cannot prove that the actor was authorized to approve the specific project and pack.
items.builder_discretion: Bind approval to a typed principal and authorization receipt scoped to project, pack hash, action, and decision time.

evidence.exact_quote: "Planning Wizard Approve And Build command boundary"

items.title: Redaction labels do not enforce no-secret storage
items.statement: The prose forbids secret-bearing content, but arbitrary strings remain accepted for actor refs, source refs, optional refs, and last_error_ref. redaction_profile is a declarative enum with no validation or sanitization receipt binding.
items.impact: Secrets, personal data, or raw error details can be persisted while the record still claims no_secrets.
items.builder_discretion: Use typed opaque IDs, reject inline URI credentials and raw errors, and bind a redaction-policy version and sanitization outcome.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Only non-secret refs and hashes may be persisted; project context and policy bodies are stored by ref, not inline secret-bearing content.",

items.title: Retention rules are not executable deletion contracts
items.statement: Retention depends on receipt reachability, referenced compile runs, audit closure, and supersession, but no reachability authority, transaction snapshot, tombstone, deletion ordering, privacy-erasure exception, or auditable compaction outcome is defined. Failed outbox rows are said to remain until superseded, yet the row schema has no supersession field.
items.impact: Compaction may delete live evidence or retain sensitive/error metadata indefinitely, and implementations cannot falsifiably agree on safe deletion.
items.builder_discretion: Define the authoritative roots, snapshot isolation, tombstone lifecycle, supersession link, erasure precedence, and post-delete receipt.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain with planning-run lineage, audit closure, and any GoalRun receipt that references the pack; never compact below retained receipt reachability.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain at least as long as the referenced PlanCompileRun and audit closure; failed rows retain retry lineage until superseded.",

items.title: Migration and format compatibility omit negotiation and rollback
items.statement: The pack contract requires new family versions and hash preservation, and the outbox migration creates a keyed row before publish, but neither defines reader/writer compatibility, canonical MessagePack profile, dual-read or dual-write window, collision handling for synthesized keys, cutover proof, or rollback.
items.impact: Mixed-version processes can disagree on bytes, hashes, and supported families, while a failed migration may duplicate or strand publication state.
items.builder_discretion: Specify canonical encoding rules, version negotiation, staged cutover invariants, deterministic legacy key derivation, and reversible checkpoints.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "No legacy writer is canonical; future value changes require a new family version and source-pack hash preservation.",
"migration": "Legacy unkeyed approval notes are source-lineage only; migration creates an idempotency-keyed outbox row before publishing.",

items.title: Stale-pack recovery is a prose branch without a durable state
items.statement: The registry says stale hashes block launch and route to refresh, but defines no stale reason code, state transition, responsible actor, preserved failed-attempt receipt, refresh identity, or rule for races between validation and launch.
items.impact: Callers may retry indefinitely, lose the causal failure, or launch a pack that changed after validation.
items.builder_discretion: Define a durable blocked state, typed mismatch evidence, refresh linkage, and a final CAS over all validated hashes at launch.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Read by exact key during PlanApproved/PlanCompileRun recovery; stale hashes block launch and route back to Planning Wizard refresh.",

items.title: Producer and consumer names are not binding seam contracts
items.statement: The registry names producers and consumers, but provides no operation identifiers, input/output versions, error vocabulary, delivery semantics, ownership for validation, or requirement that all listed consumers support this family version. Retention additionally names GoalRun receipts without listing that surface as a consumer.
items.impact: Cross-document implementations can each appear locally conformant while disagreeing at the read, write, replay, and retention seams.
items.builder_discretion: Bind each seam to versioned operation contracts and enumerate retention/indexing callers explicitly.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain with planning-run lineage, audit closure, and any GoalRun receipt that references the pack; never compact below retained receipt reachability.",

items.title: Outbox retry and support evidence is insufficient
items.statement: retry_count and last_error_ref are optional and there are no attempt timestamps, next-attempt time, backoff policy, maximum retries, worker identity, trace correlation, last transition time, failure class, or dead-letter state.
items.impact: Operators cannot tell whether a failed row is progressing, wedged, exhausted, safe to replay, or owned by a live worker.
items.builder_discretion: Add durable attempt/transition receipts, bounded backoff policy identity, worker claim data, failure class, and terminal quarantine semantics.

items.title: Materialized status has no runtime-truth qualification
items.statement: Both families are labeled materialized while the same registry globally forbids ordinary product work nodes and keeps the buildability gate false. The contract does not define whether materialized means schema-specified, storage-created, migration-complete, or runtime-operational.
items.impact: A UI, audit projector, or operator surface may present storage readiness as implemented or launch-ready despite the explicit global buildability prohibition.
items.builder_discretion: Define status semantics and require projections to display schema readiness separately from runtime and buildability readiness.

items.title: Offline reference availability is unspecified
items.statement: Pack bodies, project context, policies, and other content are deliberately stored by reference, but the value contract does not identify locality, pinning, availability class, cached integrity behavior, or recovery when a referenced object is unavailable during offline or network-loss operation.
items.impact: A locally durable pack may be unreadable or unlaunchable after network loss even though its registry row validates and remains retained.
items.builder_discretion: Type refs by storage locality and require availability/pinning state plus a deterministic unavailable-reference failure and recovery path.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Only non-secret refs and hashes may be persisted; project context and policy bodies are stored by ref, not inline secret-bearing content.",

items.title: Structural schemas do not provide semantic acceptance oracles
items.statement: The strict object shapes are machine-testable, but the registry supplies no executable oracle for hash correctness, referential existence, cross-field consistency, legal outbox transitions, crash replay, retention reachability, or producer-consumer version agreement.
items.impact: Tests can prove JSON shape while missing the failure modes that determine correctness of approval and publication.
items.builder_discretion: Define invariant tests and fault-injection scenarios with durable expected receipts for each transition and crash boundary.

items.title: Buildability and generation scope are explicitly constrained
items.statement: The registry directly prevents these value contracts from being interpreted as authorization for ordinary product work nodes or node seeds and fixes the scope to Tier 0C-2 storage value contracts.

items.title: Unknown object fields are rejected
items.statement: Both value schemas close their object shapes with additionalProperties false, reducing silent forward-field acceptance and misspelled-field persistence.

items.title: Required pack lineage and policy hashes are explicit
items.statement: The approved pack requires planning identity, revisions, index hashes, context and testing policy hashes, audit closure hash, actor, source refs, and redaction profile rather than leaving these entirely optional.

items.title: Outbox status and redaction vocabularies are bounded
items.statement: The outbox schema limits status and redaction_profile to enumerated values, preventing arbitrary state labels even though transition and enforcement semantics remain gaps.

dimension_assessments.summary: Named producer and consumer labels lack versioned seam contracts, and retention introduces an additional GoalRun reachability caller.
Outbox enums exist, but legal transitions and status-dependent field invariants do not.
Pack version mutation and outbox sequence or worker ownership lack CAS, uniqueness, and claim semantics.
The redb-and-seglog publication boundary has no crash-consistency or reconciliation protocol.
Stale-pack refresh is not a durable typed recovery path, and migration rollback is absent.
A free-form actor ref and actorless outbox cannot prove approval authority.
Declarative redaction labels do not prevent secret-bearing arbitrary refs, and retention lacks erasure precedence.
Weak digest, idempotency, and reference types accept ambiguous or adversarial values.
Materialized can be projected as operational readiness even while buildability is required to remain false.
Reference locality, pinning, and unavailable-reference recovery are not specified.
Reference arrays and strings are unbounded, and retry processing has no budget or backoff ceiling.

The authoritative core is a storage-value registry and defines no end-user interaction, focus, input, visual, auditory, or assistive-technology behavior; misleading readiness projection is assessed separately.
The core stores machine identifiers, hashes, refs, enums, and UTC timestamps and specifies no user-facing localized content; arbitrary error bodies are expressly intended to remain by reference.
Family-version and legacy-row prose lacks encoding profile, negotiation, cutover, and rollback details.
Outbox retries and transitions lack timing, ownership, trace, failure-class, and exhaustion evidence.
Compaction and retention are not expressed as safe, auditable, race-resistant deletion operations.
Owner and consumer references identify intended documents or components but do not bind operation versions or validation responsibilities.
Closed structural schemas are testable, but correctness-critical semantic and fault-recovery invariants have no executable oracles.
The most consequential residual uncertainty is the undefined meaning of materialized across schema, storage, migration, and runtime truth, compounded by opaque reference availability.
